faq.q: What is the significance of the 1.52 times subscription?
faq.a: A 1.52 times subscription means that investors applied for 1.52 shares for every 1 share offered in the IPO. While it indicates that demand exceeded supply, it's considered a moderate oversubscription, suggesting decent but not overwhelming investor interest in the company.

faq.q: How quickly will I receive a refund if I don't get an allotment?
faq.a: If you applied through the ASBA facility and are not allotted shares, the blocked amount in your bank account is typically unblocked within 1-3 working days following the finalisation of the allotment.

faq.q: Can I check my allotment status without a PAN number?
faq.a: Generally, a PAN number is a mandatory identifier for checking IPO allotment status on official registrar and exchange websites. It is linked to your demat account and application. Without it, checking status can be challenging.

faq.q: What should I do if my shares are not credited or refund not received?
faq.a: If you faced an issue, first re-check your application details. Then, contact the IPO registrar (KFin Technologies for Mahanadi Coalfields) directly. If the issue persists, you can escalate it to your depository participant or SEBI.

faq.q: Is it advisable to sell shares on the listing day?
faq.a: The decision to sell on listing day depends on your investment goals, the listing premium, and your outlook on the company's long-term prospects. Some investors prefer to book immediate profits, while others hold for potential long-term growth.

faq.q: What is the role of the Registrar (KFin Technologies) in the IPO process?
faq.a: The Registrar, KFin Technologies in this case, is responsible for accurately processing all IPO applications, determining the basis of allotment, crediting shares to successful applicants' demat accounts, and processing refunds for unallotted applications.
